All now use the verified 331M shares and ~$0.885B net claims, and agent_5's NAV arithmetic error is already fixed. No remaining input error warrants adjusting any agent. The result is ~18% below the $11.35 spot.

thesis_triggers.event: At ~$6.2 the equity is ~$2.05B on ~331M shares. Adding ~$0.885B of net claims at close gives an EV of ~$2.9B, which covers roughly uranium plus VAC at a discount to cost and nothing for the REE upstream, Donald or ASM. A sustained close there would mean something broke: the VAC close failed or Berlin imposed conditions that gut the economics, the conditional OSC loan fell through and forced a large discounted equity raise, or uranium fell below ~$65/lb. This is the forecasters' mean (range 6.0-6.3), and I did not change it.

supervisor_summary: Energy Fuels ($11.35) is a low-cost US uranium producer turning into a leveraged, stock-funded mine-to-magnet platform. After the early-2027 VAC close it will have ~331M shares and ~$0.885B of net claims, and the $725M OSC loan that would fund REE capex is still only conditional. The revised forecasts now agree on the capital structure, and my checks found no remaining factual error. The reconciled fair value is ~$9.3 (~18% below spot), and I kept the mean ladder (P(close >= $11.35) = 0.45, median ~$10.4, thesis break $6.2). Near-term swing factors are the Trump-Xi summit and the Jan-10 truce expiry, German FDI conditions on VAC, and whether the OSC loan finalizes before an equity raise is needed.
key_drivers: Capital structure after the VAC close (expected early 2027): ~331M basic shares, ~$0.75B net debt plus up to $135M Ara preferred (~$0.885B net claims), $700M converts at a $20.34 conversion price, and a 19.9% Ara holder overhang
VAC economics and approval: ~$2.04B EV for $29M 2025 adj. EBITDA. 2027 EBITDA is likely $60-90M. The German FDI review is formally open with conditions expected but no block
Funding of REE capex: the $725M OSC loan is still only a conditional commitment. If it fails, only ~$95M of cash is left after close, which implies an equity raise
Uranium: spot ~$90/lb and LT $96.50 (record), ~$23/lb production cost. This is the cash-generating floor
US-China rare-earth policy: the Busan truce runs to 2027-01-10 and a Trump-Xi summit is pending. Thaw headlines have deflated the scarcity premium, and new export controls could re-inflate it quickly
